title: Market-entry slate & channel-ready go-to-market checklist for new model
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Provide a compact, channel-aware checklist and acceptance criteria for adding a new model to Redwood's catalog. This ticket coordinates marketing, docs, benchmarks, engineering rollout gating, and partner enablement so launches are consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope: Catalog entry, perf/quality benchmarks, SDK/REST example updates, release notes, localized announcements, sales/partner brief, and runtime rollout policy. Not responsible for model training or upstream OS licensing (handled by Model-Onboarding PR).

Pre-launch (gates - owners in parentheses):
- Catalog metadata & assets (PM): model description, short blurb, intended use-cases, limitations, recommended prompt patterns, sample prompts per vertical (2–3). Include privacy/PII notes and data retention statement. Acceptance: metadata passes content QA and legal quick-check.
- Benchmarks (Research/ML): perf matrix for throughput/latency/cost (p95/p50), quality evals vs baseline on our canonical eval set, hallucination/error rate estimates. Produce CSV and PNG artifacts. Acceptance: public latency/cost numbers within 20% of verified runtime tests; quality regressions flagged with example prompts.
- SDK & API samples (DevRel/SDK): update JS/Python snippets, streaming example, and tool-calling pattern if applicable. Acceptance: examples run with smoke script against staging. GitHub PR: link in comments.
- Console & Catalog UI (Design/Console PM): listing copy, screenshots, badge for tiering (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), tags for recommended workloads. Acceptance: staging preview and UX acceptance by 1 designer + PM.
- Release notes & changelog (PM + Docs): single-page release note, changelog entry, short 'what's new' TL;DR and 'migration notes' if API changes. Acceptance: approved by docs owner.
- Legal & Security (Legal/Security): license check, export controls, KMS compatibility note, data handling statement. Acceptance: legal sign-off or explicit ok in comments.
- Pricing & SKU (RevOps/PM): recommended pricing band, token-cost estimate and expected unit economics. Acceptance: RevOps confirms SKU and billing codes.
- Field & Sales enablement (Solutions, Sales Ops): short pitch deck (1–2 slides), FAQ, known limitations & comparison to adjacent catalog models. Acceptance: slide deck uploaded and PRD link included.
- Regionalization & localization (PM/Localization): translated short blurb for EU/APAC markets, regional endpoints guidance, data residency notes. Acceptance: translation for EN/FR/DE/JP as needed for initial markets.
- Monitoring & SLOs (Engineering/Observability): dashboard templates, traceable examples for per-model latency/cost SLOs, alert runbooks. Acceptance: dashboards in staging and alert test executed.

Launch-day checklist (day-of):
- Final smoke test against production endpoints (QA/Eng): generate sample prompts across workloads, verify streaming, quantization variant fallbacks.
- Publish catalog entry & release notes (PM + Docs): push to production catalog, mark release notes live.
- Email/announcements (Growth/Comms): schedule customer email, partner briefing, and social assets. Have copy and tracking UTM parameters.
- Monitor first-hour metrics (SRE/PM): p95 latency, error rate, egress cost per 1k tokens, any spikes in KV cache hit/miss. Runbook owners on-call.
- Support readiness (Support): upload troubleshooting KB and expected symptom list; set up triage channel (Slack).

Post-launch (0–14 days):
- Collect telemetry & early indicators (PM/Research): compare real traffic to benchmark dataset; call out any divergence and file a follow-up ENG ticket if quality regressions detected.
- Fix backlog & rollouts (Eng/PM): address critical bugs, adjust rollout percentage per rollout policy.
- Update docs & tutorials (Docs/DevRel): add community examples, notebook demos, and sample prompt gallery.
- Sales/Customer feedback loop (Solutions/PM): collect top 10 field questions and update FAQ; schedule debrief.

Rollout policy & fallback: default is canary 10% traffic for first 24h, 50% next 72h if health metrics are green, otherwise automatic rollback to a compatible variant. Explicitly list compatible fallback model(s) in catalog metadata.

Acceptance criteria for "Done":
- Catalog entry live with approved metadata and assets.
- Benchmarks uploaded and linked in catalog entry.
- SDK examples and release notes published.
- Legal & security sign-off noted in ticket.
- Field enablement materials available and distributed to Sales and Partners.
- Monitoring dashboards and alerts active.

Links & artifacts (placeholders to be replaced with real links):
- Model PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRD/New+Model+X
- Benchmark CSV & PNG: drive.google.com/drive/folders/benchmark-model-x
- SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4321
- Console preview: https://console-staging.redwood.ai/catalog/model-x
- Release notes template: https://docs.redwood.ai/release-notes/template

Notes, tradeoffs and open questions:
- Should we publish a small 'beta' tag for Hosted-only launches before Dedicated/Private availability? Pros: faster time-to-market; Cons: potential customer confusion and support burden. (PM to decide by EOD -2026-02-09)
- Quantization guidance: ship with FP16 baseline and recommend 4-bit quantized variant for Dedicated if available. Engineering to confirm memory/cost delta.
- Benchmarks vs. competitor: include one normalized 'cost-per-token' row for transparency; ensure legal clearance for comparative claims.
